triage.note: Two findings from the G1 audits meet here. (1) The contract fixes the doc_status derivation order as non-negotiable -- 'unusable input / normalization collapse -> failed' is tested FIRST, 'not a detectable 10-K -> unsupported' second -- and extract.py has them the other way round: the ACCEPTED_FORMS test runs before the COLLAPSE_FLOOR test. (2) No case in the suite produced 'failed' at all, so COLLAPSE_FLOOR and the entire failed branch were untested; the one case that permitted it (malformed-html) accepts three statuses and actually returns 'ambiguous'. A contract status with no eval representation is decorative -- the same defect ADR-005 was written to fix for 'omitted'. This is not pedantry about ordering: the two statuses are different diagnoses shown to a user. 'failed' says we could not read this document, which sends them to re-download it; 'unsupported' says this is not a 10-K, which sends them to check the wrong thing entirely. For the T7 upload path, where a truncated or interrupted download is the single most likely bad input a real user will supply, telling them the wrong thing is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one.

provenance: SELF-CREATED adversarial fixture: the first 1,200 bytes of evals/fixtures/aapl-2026-10q/filing.htm (Apple Inc. Q1 FY2026 10-Q -- see that fixture's README row for original public-source provenance), truncated 2026-08-16 with no other modification. The cut lands inside markup, exactly as an interrupted HTTP transfer or a partial file copy leaves a file. The source is a 10-Q rather than a 10-K deliberately: this fixture must be BOTH collapsed AND unidentifiable as a 10-K, because that is the only input shape where the contract's fixed ordering and the implemented ordering disagree. A truncated 10-K whose <TYPE> declaration survives the cut already returns 'failed' today (verified while authoring: a 1,200-byte prefix of premier-pacific-2016 keeps form_type_declared '10-K', passes the ACCEPTED_FORMS test, and reaches the collapse test) -- so a fixture built that way would have gone green on arrival and proved nothing about the ordering. MEASURED EFFECT (run 2026-08-16 against the T5 pipeline, before any fix): meta.norm_chars 13, form_type None, form_type_declared None, form_type_sniffed None, doc_status 'unsupported'. Thirteen characters of normalized text is an unambiguous collapse by any threshold -- COLLAPSE_FLOOR is 2,000 -- and the run still reports the input as an unrecognised form rather than an unreadable one. WHY THESE CHECKS: doc_status value 'failed' (exact, not an 'in' list) is the assertion under test and is red today at 'unsupported'; an 'in' list here would defeat the purpose, since the whole finding is that two statuses are being confused. warning_present('normalization_collapse') pins the REASON as well as the label, so a future change cannot satisfy the case by returning 'failed' for some unrelated cause -- and it is one of only three warning_present rows in the whole suite, which was itself an audit finding (four of six validators still have no case proving they fire; that debt is tracked in the G1 ledger row, not closed here). only_items([]) enforces the contract's refusal rule: 'unsupported'/'failed' mean the pipeline refused, and it must never emit a best-effort items parse of a document it could not read. no_empty_success is the counterpart -- it would fire if a future change made this input report success with nothing in it. Tagged 'invariant' because refusing honestly, and refusing with the right diagnosis, is not allowed to regress. NOT yet dual-passed by extraction-auditor: pending, per case-authoring step 8.
